C0.quote: agents dynamically form coalitions around proposals that they prefer over the status quo
C0.note: Deliberative coalition formation to identify a most-supported proposal; a collective-decision process, computational and social-choice flavour. Borderline but treated as eligible.

C1.quote: the deliberation process is guaranteed to terminate
C1.note: Main results are termination bounds and guarantees of success for transition types in metric spaces. These are algorithmic/dynamics results; no AX/SB/EQ/WD category fits well. OT covers the conceptual deliberation model.

C2.1.value: approval set; supports a proposal (no ballot term)
C2.1.quote: the set X v is the approval set of v

C2.2.quote: when x >v r we say that v approves x
C2.2.note: Agents' approval of proposals over the status quo; each agent supports a single proposal.

C2.3.quote: whether she (strictly) prefers x over the status quo r
C2.3.note: Agents have locations in a metric space and preferences over proposals.

C2.4.quote: x >v r if and only if ρ(v, x) < ρ(v, r)
C2.4.note: Approval is derived directly from held location/preference. Only in the conclusion is truthful revelation mentioned, with no statement of reason.

C3.1.quote: in our current model agents are not strategic
C3.1.note: Strategic extension left for future work.

C3.2.quote: they truthfully reveal whether they support a given proposal

C3.3.note: No reason is given for truthful revelation.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or satisfaction notion is used for voters; only preference over status quo.

C5.1.quote: the set of most-supported alternatives is M ∗
C5.1.note: Success is defined as identifying the proposal with maximum support, a popularity/support criterion. Borderline: support count is not literally welfare or efficiency; coded Y as a representation/support criterion.

C5.2.quote: x >v r if and only if ρ(v, x) < ρ(v, r)
C5.2.note: Support is evaluated on approval derived from agents' held locations in the metric space.

VOT.quote_behav: we assume that agents are driven by a desire to get behind a winning proposal
VOT.note: Agents myopically move to larger coalitions, but the conclusion says agents are not strategic. Chosen: behaviour follows fixed myopic rules (NONSTRAT would also fit); STRAT is the first-listed fit only if goal-driven. Doubt: the conclusion says 'agents are not strategic', so NONSTRAT is the better reading.

CAN.note: Proposals are alternatives; proposers are not separately modelled.

ORG.note: An external mediator is mentioned but takes no action in the model.

C8.1.quote: a deliberation that consists of single-agent transitions
C8.1.note: Agents' goal-driven moves are best-response-like coalition dynamics. If VOT is read as NONSTRAT, C8 would be NA.

claims.quote: formal foundations for the design and development of practical systems
theoretical foundations for the analysis of deliberative processes

C9.1.note: Claims about real deliberation platforms such as LiquidFeedback or Polis.

C9.2.quote: systems that can support successful deliberation
C9.2.note: Applying the results to real platforms needs agents' truthful reporting of approval and myopic behaviour. Truthfulness is stated only in the conclusion, and the metric-space preference model is an unstated link to real preferences.
